precedence

/PRESS-uh-dens/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Precedence means the condition of being treated as more important than someone or something else — first place in importance or order.

At the space agency, safety checks always take precedence over the launch schedule.

Example

In the emergency room, patients with life-threatening injuries take precedence over those with sprained ankles, no matter who arrived first.

The severe cases are ranked as more important and are treated first — that ranking of importance is precedence. Notice the standard phrase 'take precedence over.'

Your Turn

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

priority: A priority is the thing a person or plan ranks first — you finish your top priority before anything else. Precedence names the relation itself: the state of coming ahead of something in importance or order, as when safety takes precedence over speed. A priority is what you rank first; precedence is the ranking.

primacy: Primacy is the settled condition of holding first place — scholars debate the primacy of one theory over another. It describes a standing status. Precedence is more transactional: it says which of two competing claims gets handled first, here and now, as when safety checks take precedence over a schedule.

superiority: Superiority means being higher or better than others in quality, strength, or status — a team can show clear superiority. It is about being above, not about going first. Precedence is strictly about order: what gets dealt with before what, regardless of which is better.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

afterthought: something pushed to the back and treated as less important

insignificance: the state of lacking importance

Where it sits · how much power over what comes first — preference → precedence → supremacy

preference vs. precedence: Preference is weaker: a preference is just a mild liking, while precedence is a real ranking that decides what comes first.

supremacy vs. precedence: Supremacy is stronger: supremacy means total dominance over everything else, while precedence simply means ranking ahead in importance or order.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — pre-

Prefix — pre-: before, in advance (Latin prae-)

Root — ced

Root — ced: to go, to yield (Latin cedere)

Suffix — -ence

Suffix — -ence: forms a noun of state or quality

Put it together

Put it together: Pre- (before) + ced- (from Latin cedere, to go): whatever has precedence literally 'goes before' everything else in importance or order.

Use the root in a new word: concede

Use the root in a new word: concede: After the recount, the candidate finally picked up the phone to concede.

Word Choice

Formal

Nearly always appears in the phrase 'take(s) precedence over.' Don't confuse it with precedent — a past example used as a guide for later decisions — which is a different word taught elsewhere in this unit.
